text: A Service Bus message is delivered 10 times and abandoned each time. Where does it end up, and with what reason?

options.text: The transfer dead-letter queue, reason TTLExpiredException

explanation: When the delivery count exceeds the maximum (default 10) the message is moved to the dead-letter queue with the reason MaxDeliveryCountExceeded. This cannot be disabled, only raised.

text: What is the default Max delivery count of a Service Bus queue or subscription?
explanation: The default is 10.

text: A message handler needs 7 minutes. What should you do?

options.text: Renew the message lock while processing, because the maximum lock duration is 5 minutes
Set the lock duration to 7 minutes
Increase the max delivery count to 7

explanation: The default lock duration is 1 minute and the maximum is 5 minutes, so longer work requires renewing the lock (for example with AutoLockRenewer).

text: What is the main risk of receive-and-delete mode in Service Bus?

options.text: If the receiver crashes after the broker sends the message, the message is lost

explanation: In receive-and-delete the message is considered settled when sent. A failed transfer or crash loses it. Peek-lock settles explicitly.

text: A receiver calls abandon_message for a message. What happens?

options.text: The lock is released immediately, the message is redelivered and its delivery count increases
The message moves to the DLQ at once

explanation: Abandon releases the lock so the message can be redelivered, incrementing the delivery count.

text: Messages for each customer must be processed in order, one customer at a time per receiver. What do you enable?

options.text: Sessions, using the customer id as the session id

explanation: Sessions provide ordered, FIFO handling per session id, and a receiver locks a whole session.

text: Where is the dead-letter queue of a topic subscription addressed?

options.text: A separate queue you must create

explanation: Each subscription has its own DLQ. Topics themselves have none, because messages are forwarded to subscriptions within milliseconds.

text: Your code completes a message after closing the receiver. What is the result?

options.text: The settlement fails; the lock expires, the message is redelivered and eventually dead-lettered if this repeats
Nothing, the SDK reopens the receiver
The message moves to the transfer DLQ

explanation: Settle before closing the receiver or connection. After closing, settlement does not reach the service and repeated redelivery ends in MaxDeliveryCountExceeded.

text: Which are dead-letter reasons set by Service Bus itself? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: The system sets reasons such as MaxDeliveryCountExceeded, TTLExpiredException (when dead-lettering on expiration is on), HeaderSizeExceeded and MaxTransferHopCountExceeded. LockRenewed is not a reason.

text: How long do messages remain in a dead-letter queue?

options.text: Until you explicitly receive them from the DLQ and complete them

explanation: There is no automatic cleanup of the DLQ and time to live is not observed there.

text: A job message may be delivered twice. How do you make processing safe?

options.text: Make the handler idempotent, for example by tracking processed message_id values

explanation: Delivery is at-least-once under peek-lock, so handlers must be idempotent. A unique message_id is the usual deduplication key.

text: What is the default retry policy of Azure Event Grid event subscriptions?

options.text: 30 maximum attempts and a 1440 minute (24 hour) time to live

explanation: The default maximum number of attempts is 30 and the default event time-to-live is 1440 minutes. Delivery stops when either limit is reached first.

text: An Event Grid webhook endpoint responds with HTTP 400 for an event. What does Event Grid do?

options.text: Does not retry; it dead-letters the event if configured, otherwise drops it

explanation: 400 (Bad Request) and 413 (Request Entity Too Large) mean delivery can never succeed, so the event is scheduled for dead-lettering immediately.

text: You must keep events that Event Grid could not deliver. What do you configure on the event subscription?

options.text: A Service Bus topic as the retry store
A Blob Storage container as the dead-letter destination
Nothing, dead-lettering is on by default

explanation: Dead-lettering is off by default and undeliverable events are dropped. Enable it by specifying a storage account container.

text: Which HTTP status codes does Event Grid treat as successful delivery? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Only 200, 201, 202, 203 and 204 are success. All other codes, including 3xx, are failures.

text: A handler must receive only OrderPlaced events where data.total is greater than 100. How do you do this with the least code?

options.text: Event type filter plus an advanced filter on data.total (NumberGreaterThan 100) on the subscription

explanation: Subscription filters (event types, subject filters and advanced filters on data fields) run in Event Grid so the handler only receives matching events.

text: What is true about Event Grid batch delivery?

options.text: It is off by default; when enabled it is all or none per batch, with up to 5,000 events per batch

explanation: By default one event is sent per request. Batching is optional, supports 1 to 5,000 events and has all-or-none semantics.

text: Which statement about Event Grid delivery guarantees is correct?

options.text: At least once, with no ordering guarantee

explanation: Event Grid delivers at least once and does not guarantee order, so subscribers must tolerate duplicates and reordering.

text: How many triggers can one Azure Function have?
explanation: A function has exactly one trigger. It can have several input and output bindings.

text: A function app must read from Service Bus using its managed identity and no connection string. Which app setting do you add?

options.text: ServiceBusConnection__fullyQualifiedNamespace=shop-bus.servicebus.windows.net, plus a data role assignment for the identity

explanation: For identity-based connections the setting named by the binding's connection property gets a __fullyQualifiedNamespace suffix, and the identity needs the appropriate Service Bus data role.

text: Which file configures a Function app for local development only and is NOT deployed to Azure?
explanation: local.settings.json holds local settings and is not published. In Azure the values come from application settings.

text: A Cosmos DB trigger Function needs which extra resource to work?

options.text: A lease container, because the trigger runs the change feed processor

explanation: The Cosmos DB trigger uses the change feed processor, which stores progress in a lease container.

text: An HTTP-triggered function uses authorization level FUNCTION. What must callers send?
explanation: FUNCTION requires a function-specific key. ADMIN requires the master key and ANONYMOUS requires none.

text: You need an event-driven serverless Function plan that scales to zero and supports virtual network integration. Which plan?
explanation: Flex Consumption is the serverless plan that scales per function, scales to zero and supports virtual networks. Premium keeps pre-warmed instances and does not scale to zero.
